source_title: read/write switch2 save data through a ns2jb session. run lua inside lullaby without a switch 1. - GitHub
source_excerpt:
read, back up, restore and modify save data for any Switch 2 title , whether it is installed, on a card, or has no card inserted, over a live ns2jb session. the save path is not game-specific: it opens a title's save archive, moves files in or out, commits, and verifies by hash.
the same access is then used for one more thing: an Artemis save can be retargeted so the game resumes our Lua instead of its own script. that is the "save launch" half ( payloads/ , tools/artemis-save.py ); the save half works on any title you own.
the kit also installs external launchers from pinned releases, including Balatro's Lua launcher for the Switch 1 edition on a Switch 2. its save files are downloaded and verified at install time.
the exploit is not here. nothing in this repo is exploit code, keys, or game content.
a patched ns2jb checkout (the local ~/ns2jb-rpc checkout, or run.cjs from ns2jb), an exploit session held open, and the run folder it prints ( runs/switch2-XXXXXX , containing switch2/ro/root/current-root.json ).
firmware 23.0.1 and SmileBASIC 4 (retail) to deliver the exploit.
the patch step is not optional; skip it only if the checkout already has the changes. docs/PATCHED-ENGINE.md explains what each patch fixes.
tools/kit.cjs adds no save logic of its own: it shells out to the proven scripts and prints the exact command before each one.
read-only by default; a write needs a prior backup and compares the live bytes against it before replacing anything;
only titles on the allowlist ( config/titles.json , plus your config/titles.local.json ) can be written;
one open, one commit, then every file is read back and hashed;
single-file root tools require /name ; installer/stage paths are validated separately and may include the subdirectories their payload requires.
Elden Ring ( 0400f5802371e000 ) is on the write allowlist. Large save files are verified in 256 KiB reads, including the game's 2.5 MiB character files.
several save operations per boot usually work; restart the console only if one actually fails. the one thing that reliably breaks the next session is leaving a previous one open ( --keep-open , a diagnostic only).
titles are listed from every storage ncm has a database for (internal, sd card, game card), and named from the console's own control data, not from a catalogue: that is the only way a switch 2 title gets a name. the name comes out of the title's control NCA (the read ouncecake falls back to; its ns reader did not answer on this console), so a japanese title can carry its japanese name. names are cached in config/titles.nacp.json ; --no-names skips the read.
ncm's list is the application list; the save store is a different index. save-inventory.cjs asks fs:srv for every save archive directly, so a title whose card is out (or whose program was removed) can still have its save listed and pulled. that is also why a cartridge save survives without the cartridge.
is the 16-byte account uid in hex; --list-uids prints them. the pull prints mounted space=… type=… uid=… - read that line, it is how you learn that the right archive opened. save-inventory.cjs is the no-catalogue path: it lists every archive in the save index and writes JSON; pull-inventory.cjs pulls exact identities from it, five at a time by default ( --limit 0 = all pending), and resumes from inventory-progress.json after a reboot. docs/RESTORE.md covers the restore path and its limits; docs/SAVE-ARCHIVES.md covers which archive an open selects.
an Artemis slot save stores where execution resumes. retarget that pointer at save:/name.asb and the game resumes there; an ASB is a plain Lua container, so a few commands put our chunk in front of the engine. a second, zero-edit entry point is the suspend file: save_prefix="save" + save_suspend=9999 makes the game look for save9999.dat at boot.
docs/LAUNCHER.md - the chain, what is proven on hardware, what is blocked.
tools/build-untethered.sh - build the stub + body + suspend launcher from a backup; tools/inject-launcher.sh - backup, build, write, pull and verify.
the stub/body split is built and smoke-tested, not yet installed on hardware.
alula's Artemis Launcher (a separate launcher)
alula/switch-artemis-launcher is a different thing from the payload above: a boot menu with a Hello World slot, an HTTP Lua server on port 8080 and a 2.lua update mechanism. kit option 8 installs it into a supported demo save; option 4 is unchanged.
supported titles: 010042d022aea000 (Seedsow demo) and 010012900d38a000 (Nora 2 demo). full games and other titles are refused.
the pinned upstream revision is downloaded at install time and every file is checked against a recorded SHA-256; nothing third-party is bundled.
it writes 7 files: six upstream scripts/font plus a save9999.dat rebuilt from the game's own suspend save, so no older upstream save container is written over yours. saveg.dat and system.dat are not touched.
both launchers own save9999.dat , so only one can be the boot path at a time. the editor's files are not touched and do not collide.
docs/ARTEMIS-LAUNCHER.md has the compatibility matrix, the 2026-11-01 hardware report (firmware 23.0.1, Seedsow demo 1.0.0), the backup/restore evidence and the known limits - including that the minus-at-startup update bypass was not observed on demo 1.0.0.
Luminger/balatro-switch-rce replaces Balatro's startup with a status console, Lua RPC and FTP. The kit's Install Balatro Lua launcher , Verify Balatro Lua launcher , and Restore Balatro gameplay entries appear only for the Switch 1 title 0100cd801ce5e000 , including that edition running on Switch 2 in compatibility mode. The native Switch 2 edition is unsupported.
pins upstream v1.1.0 by archive and per-file SHA-256; adds 20 launcher files under /.lovegame/ and excludes the ZIP's JKSV metadata;
takes a fresh live backup, preserves gameplay files and records an immutable original baseline and receipt before writing; existing launcher paths are refused;
rollback takes another backup and removes only receipt-owned launcher files, preserving profiles, settings, logs and unrelated files;
upstream documents Switch 1 builds 1.0.1f and 1.0.1o ; its hardware report covers its JKSV/save-transfer route. This direct SaveKit installation and rollback still need a hardware smoke test.
See docs/BALATRO-LAUNCHER.md for offline staging and dry runs, compatibility, receipt recovery, and the unauthenticated RPC/FTP ports.
The installed Artemis Launcher serves /status , /eval , /save and /delete on port 8080. tools/artemis-http.cjs uses only those endpoints, so it works while the game is running and no RPC session is held :
downloads are bounded /eval hex reads with chunk hashes, a final SHA-256, resume state and local atomic promotion;
uploads are direct /save up to the server body cap, or chunked /eval appends above it (non-atomic: os.rename on save:/ is refused on hardware); the reported hash is read back from the console and compared, and an interrupted upload is reported as incomplete;
the backup is explicit-file, complete:false - the server has no directory listing - so it cannot authorize a destructive full restore;
protected launcher files are refused for write/delete, and other titles' saves are not reachable.
Full details, hardware results (4/16/64 KiB, binary, relaunch) and limitations: docs/ARTEMIS-HTTP.md .
the controller/esp32 work lives in ns2-console ; the content/asset pipeline is in ns2-assets .
our code is MIT (see LICENSE ). third-party components and links are listed in NOTICE : ns2jb (the exploit, linked not vendored), Seedsow Lua Editor (0BSD; its save is downloaded, never bundled), titledb (MIT, names only), and the Artemis engine (no affiliation, no game content).
